title: Carbon Nanotubes with Springs Morphologies Produced from Iron Catalyst
content: The properties of carbon nanotubes and their applications are still being studied. In recent years, the production of carbon nanotubes (CNT) has been carried out by three different techniques: arc discharge between two graphite electrodes [1-5] chemical vapor deposition (CVD) [6-10] and; Laser ablation [11-13]. Both laser ablation and arc discharge produce high-quality SWNT. Among the methods presented, CVD is the most adaptable method for large-scale CNT production at a lower cost [6]. In the CVD method, the first role of the catalyst is to decompose the hydrocarbon molecules and then promote the formation of CNT [14, 15]. The control of the production, selectivity and quality of CNT comes from the combination of the properties of the catalysts and the real parameters. Thus, this project aims to synthesize and investigate new catalysts for the production of carbon nanotubes, mainly SWNT, by the CVD method. Recently, the introduction of new strategies has customized the production of CNTs. A recent study shows how the use of a monocrystalline silicon substrate causes single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) to grow in an oriented manner, nanotubes with lengths of up to 18.5 cm [16]. The helical or spring-like morphology of CNTs has aroused great interest in the scientific field [17].
